patterns.what_worked: Direct scrapes beat search for this: Blizzard's three Russian class pages carry the spec names as plain headings, and wow.gg serves a markdown build of every Russian guide (/ru/guides/<spec>.md) whose H1 is the exact class+spec string. Eight names were confirmed from two independently fetched sources each with about a dozen requests, and only two SearXNG queries were needed to locate pages.
patterns.what_was_hard: Two sources refused to yield: the Russian warcraft.wiki.gg paths redirect to the English main page whether the title is raw or percent-encoded (its own redirect double-encodes the title), and wowhead.com/ru guide pages are JS-rendered so only their indexed snippets expose the names. I did not repeat either request. The more useful discovery was that Blizzard's Russian Demon Hunter page lists a THIRD spec, Пожиратель (Devourer, retail 11.2), which the table deliberately omits because the classic clients have no such spec and lib.spec_table has no third entry to align it with.
patterns.skill_gap: A name can be right and still be a trap: Пожиратель is Blizzard's own Russian string, but adding it would break the index alignment against lib.spec_table. Verification of a NAME is not verification of its POSITION, and the pin's length check is what protects that.
